scenes.text: Your most vivid memory? It's been edited at least a dozen times.
scenes.query: vintage film editing room dark lamp

scenes.text: By you. And you approved every cut… without reading it.
scenes.query: fountain pen signing paper macro dark

scenes.text: See, you think memory works like a camera. Record the moment, store the file, play it back.
scenes.query: vintage film camera reel spinning close

scenes.text: You've never watched the raw footage. The raw footage is gone.
scenes.query: empty film reel dust dark table

scenes.text: But he cuts every scene of your life with one job in mind: make you the reasonable one.
scenes.query: film editor hands cutting film splicer vintage

scenes.text: That argument from three years ago? Watch his work.
Your tone — softened in the mix. Their tone — punched up.
scenes.query: audio mixing console faders hands close

scenes.text: That thing you said, the cruel one, the one that actually started it?
scenes.query: face profile half shadow dark portrait

scenes.text: Every retelling, another pass. Your version gets smoother. Cleaner. More you.
scenes.query: film reels spinning projector room dark

scenes.text: That's why the story you've told twenty times feels truer than ever — it's had twenty rounds of post-production.
scenes.query: projector beam dust particles dark room

scenes.text: 'So how do I know which memories are real?' You run the test.
A memory that's only checked against your other memories? That's the editor grading his own film — of course it holds together, he cut it that way.
scenes.query: magnifying loupe film negatives light table

scenes.text: The text messages from that night. The other person's version. The friend who was standing right there. Evidence from outside the edit.
scenes.query: hands phone screen glow dark night

scenes.text: And when the outside footage contradicts your director's cut? That flinch you just felt — that's him, reaching for the scissors.

scenes.query: eyes close up serious low light

scenes.text: Because here's the final cut: the story of your life is a true story… …based on actual events.
